cover_hook: 150 years on, a mystery skeleton may have a name
caption_hook: 💀 A skeleton found in a Roman coffin at Westminster Abbey in 1869 may finally have a name: a medieval abbot + 3 more wins 👇
question: Which would you rather see in person: 🏰 the abbey coffin or ☄️ the new comet?
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves a good mystery
reel_hook: 150 years on, a mystery skeleton may have a name
first_comment: Bonus: the coffin was made for a wealthy Roman Briton, Valerius Amandinus, whose name is still carved on it. About 600 years later, someone else was put inside. Who would you guess? 🏰

stories.stat_label: the year the coffin was dug up
stories.headline: Westminster Abbey's mystery skeleton may be a medieval abbot
stories.summary: The skeleton in a Roman stone coffin dates to 987-1052 AD, centuries after the coffin was made. An expert now names 2 abbots who fit: Ælfwig, who died around 1020, or Wulfnoth.
stories.why: New tests found he was 35-49 years old, not under 30 as Victorians thought.

stories.headline: A galaxy-mapping telescope found its 1st comet by accident
stories.summary: Euclid wasn't built to hunt comets, but a PhD student's software spotted one streaking through 5 sets of its images. The comet is about 1.3 billion km away and loops over the solar system.
stories.why: Its orbit takes thousands of years, so this may be its 1st visit since telescopes were invented.

stories.stat_label: strikes of a stick to save a friend
stories.headline: A forest worker fought off a tiger with a stick to save his friend
stories.summary: On patrol in Corbett, Ramnath turned to see a tiger on top of his young colleague Pitambar. He hit it 3 times with his wooden stick; it let go, and Pitambar survived with bite wounds.
stories.why: The two are so close that Pitambar calls Ramnath 'uncle'.

stories.stat_label: months of care before going home
stories.headline: After 17 months of care, an orphaned manatee swam free
stories.summary: Cullen was hit by a boat in May 2025 alongside his mother, who didn't survive. After rehab in Miami, the Keys and Jacksonville, he was released back into the sea at Tavernier.
stories.why: He was nursed back to strength across 3 different rescue sites.

fun_fact: The Roman coffin's lid was recarved with a big cross about 1,000 years ago, a clue it had been reused.
